cases.name: portfolioActualReturn
cases.title: One reported return
cases.rests_on: What the money set aside for retirement returned over the last twelve months — not the return of everything invested. Over accounts that are not property, that have a return for the last twelve months reported by the person (a reported 0 counts; one not reported is left out, never read as 0; a reported loss of everything or more is left out), and that have some amount set aside for retirement: each account's start = the amount set aside today ÷ (1 + its return). The answer = the amounts set aside today added up ÷ the starts added up − 1 — what the money set aside grew by, each account weighed by what was set aside when the twelve months began. No answer when either total is zero or less.

cases.name: incomeBearingClassOf
cases.title: Money-market fund priority
working: Money market match is evaluated before settlement/sweep → Stocks / Funds.
cases.rests_on: From the account's name, capitals ignored, whole words only (put is not Putnam; cd is not ABCD), first match wins. Money market (also mmkt, mmf, or the ticker of a money-market fund) → Stocks / Funds — read before the sweep words, so a money-market settlement fund is the fund (the owner's rule of 2026-08-04). Each option = its value as synced, under Alternatives (an option is valued when it is synced, at contracts × price per share × 100 — owner, 2026-08-26). If the parts come to less than the balance and one or more holdings have NO price: the whole difference is filed under the unpriced holdings' class when they share one, and under Unclassified when they span classes — never under cash. Otherwise, if the parts do not add up to the balance: a difference no bigger than the larger of $1 or 1% of the balance is added to cash when positive (owner rule, 2026-08-11), or taken off the largest class when negative; a bigger one is put under the account's own class (assetClassOf). ACCOUNT BUILT BY HAND (not a cash or property account): when it records its own cash (or its balance is built from its records) and its balance is below zero, the whole balance is cash — overdrawn is negative cash: balance −$100 with a cash field of $50 is Cash −$100 (DEC-4036i, 2026-10-10). Otherwise its cash = the uninvested cash it records, above zero, never more than the balance, when its balance is built from its records or it records cash. When its balance is built from its holdings, each holding is weighed at today's value — shares × the broker's price, else the value its balance was last built from, else what was paid — and the rest of the balance is shared out among the holdings' classes by those weights, so a T-bill is Bonds & CDs; if every holding is of the account's own class, the rest stays whole under that class. No answer when it records no cash and its holdings are all of its own class. ANY OTHER ACCOUNT — a typed balance, a bank account — gets no answer. The parts always add up to the balance.

No directly governing Part 1 card identified from this rule text; this rule requires review against its other governing functions/screens. Years to maturity count calendar days, not the time of day. Before: the hour shaved part of a day off (one example moved from 5.66% to 5.65%).

No directly governing Part 1 card identified from this rule text; this rule requires review against its other governing functions/screens. The sweep that corrects classes never changes an account the person confirmed. Before: it could overwrite a confirmed class.

No directly governing Part 1 card identified from this rule text; this rule requires review against its other governing functions/screens. A saved record whose accounts were all deleted shows the first-day screen, not $0 owned. Before: it showed $0 with a 7% average return.

Related Part 1 formula card(s) are consistent with the rule as written. The retirement money’s twelve-month return weighs each account by what was set aside when the year began: Σ now ÷ Σ start − 1. Before: weighed by today’s amounts, 13.72% where 12.98% is right.

No directly governing Part 1 card identified from this rule text; this rule requires review against its other governing functions/screens. A 529’s and an HSA’s tax words are fixed by what they are; ‘(Roth)’ appears only for an account in the Roth bucket. Before: a 529 stated tax-free read ‘tax-free (Roth)’.

Related formula card(s) are flagged for correction/review: MK-NW-F-027. A hand-built account is split holding by holding, so a T-bill inside it is Bonds & CDs. Before: everything but its cash was filed under the account’s own class.

Related formula card(s) are flagged for correction/review: MK-NW-F-025. A Roth 401(k) reads Roth 401(k), and a tax-advantaged account with no kind and known digits shows its tax word. Before: ‘Fidelity 401(k)’ for both a Roth and a pre-tax 401(k); ‘Vanguard -1234’ for a Roth.

No directly governing Part 1 card identified from this rule text; this rule requires review against its other governing functions/screens. Related formula card(s) are flagged for correction/review: MK-NW-F-028. Broker Treasury wording (TREAS, UST, T-bond) counts as a Treasury in the words under an account, and more than one reads Treasuries. Before: a broker’s T-bill read ‘1 bond’.
Related Part 1 formula card(s) are consistent with the rule as written. A value dated by its month alone is shown as the 1st of that month. Before: the stored text was handed back unchanged.

No directly governing Part 1 card identified from this rule text; this rule requires review against its other governing functions/screens. Performance draws no walk for a window its record exists but cannot reach; a sentence names the record’s first day. Before: the beginning was worked back from today and wealth generated shown as if measured.

No directly governing Part 1 card identified from this rule text; this rule requires review against its other governing functions/screens. A rate the person set themselves is labelled an estimate. Before: it took the record’s flag.

No directly governing Part 1 card identified from this rule text; this rule requires review against its other governing functions/screens. An employer’s percent match is taken on the 401(k) figure after the yearly limit. Before: on the figure as typed — $1,600 where $1,490 is right.

No directly governing Part 1 card identified from this rule text; this rule requires review against its other governing functions/screens. History shared is rounded down and its sentence built from whole months only. Before: one day short of a year read ‘1 year’.

No directly governing Part 1 card identified from this rule text; this rule requires review against its other governing functions/screens. Accounts made by itemising carry the typical rate for their class, never 0%, and a bond rate not entered stays blank. Before: every itemised account had a 0% rate.

Related Part 1 formula card(s) are consistent with the rule as written. The Other investments summary reads the class split, so its total is the Alternatives line’s dollars and each part is rated by what it is. Before: whole accounts only — $18,641 where the Alternatives line read $23,031.

Related Part 1 formula card(s) are consistent with the rule as written. A property’s name is not read as evidence of its class; a fund that writes options is a fund. Before: ‘Silver Lake house’ read as an alternative and a covered-call ETF as options.

Related Part 1 formula card(s) are consistent with the rule as written. What a property is for has one reading for every function; handed the rent entries, a property is a rental only when an entry names it, and a household with no home is told so. Before: three functions read it three ways; a rented-out house marked home counted as the home.

No directly governing Part 1 card identified from this rule text; this rule requires review against its other governing functions/screens. Years to maturity are exact, by anniversaries: one year to the day is exactly 1. Before: days ÷ 365.25 (0.9993 for one year).

No directly governing Part 1 card identified from this rule text; this rule requires review against its other governing functions/screens. A bond is priced at exact times, its yearly coupon on each maturity anniversary; a matured bond or one with no date has no price. Before: years rounded to a whole number, at least 1, so a matured bond still paid.

Related Part 1 formula card(s) are consistent with the rule as written. A missing balance is never $0: it is left out of the total and the amber box names the account. Before: a linked account that failed to sync added 0 and the total looked complete.

No directly governing Part 1 card identified from this rule text; this rule requires review against its other governing functions/screens. Itemised sums are exact decimals, a holding with no value is left out, and the remainder is then not final. Before: a missing value was 0 and the remainder looked complete; sums could leave a fraction of a cent.

Related formula card(s) are flagged for correction/review: MK-NW-F-025. A kind that names contents — crypto, private equity, hedge funds, other — claims no Brokerage wrapper unless the person confirmed one. Before: ‘Coinbase Brokerage’ for a crypto wallet.

No directly governing Part 1 card identified from this rule text; this rule requires review against its other governing functions/screens. CDs, certificates of deposit and share certificates are recognised as CDs; ABCD Growth Fund is not. Before: ‘No-Penalty CDs’ was not a CD.

No directly governing Part 1 card identified from this rule text; this rule requires review against its other governing functions/screens. The accrued-interest note shows only for a bond that pays interest and has no accrued figure entered. Before: a zero-coupon bond got the note.

No directly governing Part 1 card identified from this rule text; this rule requires review against its other governing functions/screens. Dates are read as calendar dates, never shifted by a time zone; an empty date shows nothing. Before: a midnight-UTC date could show the day before in Pacific time.

The value typed for a bond is what the statement shows, which leaves out the interest earned since the last coupon. For the yield to maturity, that interest is added: the figure entered, or an estimate from the coupon schedule, and then the screen reads: "Added estimated $1,119 in accrued interest to bond value at 4.5% coupon for 363 days to calculate YTM. A $25,000 4.5% Treasury worth $24,200 two days before its coupon now reads 5.69%, not 7.44%.

No directly governing Part 1 card identified from this rule text; this rule requires review against its other governing functions/screens. When the daily record does not reach back to the window's first day, the beginning is worked back from today: today's value less what each holding gained, less the money moved. (1) A CD with a stated rate gains by its rate: value now × (1 − 1 ÷ (1 + rate) to the power of the years in the window) — $10,500 at 5% for a year gained $500. (2) A holding with no price history and no stated rate — a bond typed by hand — has a gain that cannot be known, so that account shows no beginning and no wealth generated, and a sentence names it: "The beginning can't be worked back: Treasury 2031 has no price history." Before: its gain counted $0, so the beginning read about $500 too high.

No directly governing Part 1 card identified from this rule text; this rule requires review against its other governing functions/screens. Where an account, a bank, a class or a debt on Net worth has no balance entered, the figure reads "Value not entered" — so the line says what is missing. By institution: "Ally · Value not entered". Before: "Ally · not entered", which did not say what was not entered.

No directly governing Part 1 card identified from this rule text; this rule requires review against its other governing functions/screens. A window that reaches back whole months (1M, 3M, 6M, 1Y, 2Y) starts on the same day of the earlier month, or on that month's last day when the day does not exist there. Mar 31 less one month is Feb 28; Feb 29 less a year is Feb 28. Before: the missing day rolled into the next month, so 1M from Mar 31 started Mar 3 — a 28-day window.

No directly governing Part 1 card identified from this rule text; this rule requires review against its other governing functions/screens. A rent or running-cost figure is a number. One with words in it — "about 2k" — is not read: it counts as not entered, and the rent field on the Income screen takes digits only. Before: "about 2k" was read as $2, and the property counted as a rental.

No directly governing Part 1 card identified from this rule text; this rule requires review against its other governing functions/screens. When a property's rent is not known — its rent entry is blank or unreadable, or the rent entries could not be read — the emergency fund still gives its months, counted without rent, and says so: "5 months, rent not included. Enter rent to include." Cash $10,000, essentials $2,000 a month: 5 months. Before (my recommendation, not built): no months figure at all.

No directly governing Part 1 card identified from this rule text; this rule requires review against its other governing functions/screens. Wherever the emergency fund's months are shown — Net worth, Job safety and Stress test — the same line sits with them when a property's rent is not known: "5.0 months, rent not included. Enter rent to include." Before: only Net worth carried it.

No directly governing Part 1 card identified from this rule text; this rule requires review against its other governing functions/screens. Adding a CD asks once: "Bought from the bank, or through a broker?" A bank CD's yield to maturity is its interest rate ($10,000 at 4.2% → 4.20%), and it has no if-rates-move estimate. A broker CD's yield to maturity is worked out like a bond's, from its face value, interest rate, statement value and maturity date ($10,000 face, 4.2%, worth $9,850, 2 years left → about 5.0%), and it gets the if-rates-move estimate like a bond. Before: every CD showed its interest rate as its yield to maturity — my rule of 2026-10-08, which assumed every CD was bought from a bank at face value.

No directly governing Part 1 card identified from this rule text; this rule requires review against its other governing functions/screens. A bond or CD with no maturity date entered keeps counting its interest (DEC-0332: unknown, not matured); its row reads "maturity date not entered". Treasury $10,000 at 4%, no date: $400 a year counted.

No directly governing Part 1 card identified from this rule text; this rule requires review against its other governing functions/screens. "CD" is read only from an account's own name or type, never from its institution's name. A brokerage account at "CD Capital" is not a CD.

Related Part 1 formula card(s) are consistent with the rule as written. A 529 is always tax-free for education, whatever tax setting is stored; its type decides (DEC-3035c). Before: a 529 stored "taxable" was counted as taxable while its page said tax-free.

Related Part 1 formula card(s) are consistent with the rule as written. An HSA is always pre-tax going in and tax-free for medical costs, whatever bucket it is filed in. Before: an HSA filed under Roth was counted as tax-free going in.

Related Part 1 formula card(s) are consistent with the rule as written. An account with no account type chosen is never assumed taxable: its tax reads "tax type not stated" with a tap to choose. Before: counted and shown as a taxable brokerage.

No directly governing Part 1 card identified from this rule text; this rule requires review against its other governing functions/screens. The old sign-up answer "savings or portfolio" is filed Unclassified and asked about: "Is this cash savings or investments?" (DEC-2160). Before: always Stocks / Funds at 7%.

No directly governing Part 1 card identified from this rule text; this rule requires review against its other governing functions/screens. Money left in an alternatives part that no priced holding explains is shown as "$1,500 asset type not classified" — never labelled Other or given a growth rate. Before: "Other" at 5%.

Related formula card(s) are flagged for correction/review: MK-NW-F-027. An overdrawn hand-built account is negative cash: balance −$100 with a cash field of $50 is Cash −$100. Before: Cash $0 and Unclassified −$100.

Related Part 1 formula card(s) are consistent with the rule as written. Where a vehicle's value is not entered, the car you drive is still picked among the vehicles with a value, and a line says: "Car A's value not entered — it may be the car you drive."

No directly governing Part 1 card identified from this rule text; this rule requires review against its other governing functions/screens. The retirement money on the Plan screens names an account it leaves out: "leaves out Linked 401(k) — Value not entered" (DEC-3657 wording). Before: $10,000 with no note.

Related Part 1 formula card(s) are consistent with the rule as written. Every date a person enters for a bond or CD is picked from a date picker, never typed — the Net worth account editor too (it had a typed "Matures YYYY-MM" box). The app is not launched, so no typed date exists to carry over.

No directly governing Part 1 card identified from this rule text; this rule requires review against its other governing functions/screens. Edit date", and a tap lets the person enter or correct the date with a date picker; the sentence then uses their date. Before: "a few days of history (from )".

No directly governing Part 1 card identified from this rule text; this rule requires review against its other governing functions/screens. A rent entry cannot be saved until the property it is for is picked. With no property in Net worth, the entry says "Add the property in Net worth first" and links there; an older entry with no property shows the question in amber until answered.

No directly governing Part 1 card identified from this rule text; this rule requires review against its other governing functions/screens. (15) A count written in words ("2 holdings", "3 CDs", "2 Treasuries", "1 year 6 months") takes its plural from ONE list of every word the app counts and its plural — holding/holdings, CD/CDs, Treasury/Treasuries, bond/bonds, option/options, year/years, month/months, property/properties and the rest in use. A word not on the list is refused by a test, so "2 propertys" can never ship. (6) The risk swing used by the Will my money last odds (a weighted average of each account's swing, MK-NW-F-035) is parked until the Plan module, where the table of how investment types move together is decided.

No directly governing Part 1 card identified from this rule text; this rule requires review against its other governing functions/screens. When sign-up's rent step comes after a property was entered, it asks "Which property is it?" right there, so rent entered at sign-up counts at once. With no property entered yet it keeps its line: "The rent is counted once you pick its property on the Income screen." Before: sign-up never asked, so its rent was not counted until the property was picked on the Income screen (DEC-4059d).

No directly governing Part 1 card identified from this rule text; this rule requires review against its other governing functions/screens. Sign-up asks for rent before any property can exist, so its rent step carries a door: "Add the property first ›". It opens Add an account set to Real estate; saving brings the person back to the rent step, which asks "Which property is it?"; once picked, the rent counts at once. About 3 taps plus typing, without leaving sign-up. Before: the rent was kept but counted nowhere until the person added the property in Net worth and picked it on the Income screen, about 7 taps after sign-up.

No directly governing Part 1 card identified from this rule text; this rule requires review against its other governing functions/screens. The time-weighted return counts money that arrives on a day as there for that whole day, and money taken out as gone for that whole day: that day's growth is the evening value ÷ (the previous evening's value + money added − money taken out) − 1. A new account opened with $10,000 and worth $10,050 that evening returned +0.50% that day (+$50); worth $9,800, −2.00% (−$200). Vanguard worth $50,000, $10,000 added in the morning, $60,300 that evening: +0.50% (the $300 was earned on $60,000). Before: the money counted as arriving at the end of the day — the first deposit into a new account could not be measured at all, a value below the money just added was refused as a broken record, and the Vanguard day read +0.60%.

No directly governing Part 1 card identified from this rule text; this rule requires review against its other governing functions/screens. With no debt entered, the Debts section's door reads "Add your debts ›" — the wording of the approved empty-state drawing. Before: Net worth v08 state C drew "Add a mortgage, card, or loan ›" while the empty-state drawing drew "Add your debts ›".

No directly governing Part 1 card identified from this rule text; this rule requires review against its other governing functions/screens. Where an approved drawing shows a figure that is wrong and the app is right, the drawing is left as drawn and its READ THIS FIRST box gets a line naming the figure, what the drawing shows, what is right, and why, with the arithmetic — Net worth v08 B −0.40% → −0.41%; E (Aug 4) → (Aug 11); F 7 days → 14 days; Bonds v02 years left 2y/4y/1y → 1y/3y/0y; Other investments v02 "Annuity" → "Annuities"; Holding detail v02 gain $7,400.00 + $1,957.60 → $7,384 + $1,974 in whole dollars. And the edit sheet of a home (any property) no longer asks "What's it invested in?".
